versions.release_notes:
🐛 Fixes
- German translation: with German as the system language, parts of the Settings window, the server information dialog and some window titles showed English text. The German file now has every string of the app. The server information dialog now uses the app language for its labels, expiration message and dates. The Settings, Downloads, Log Viewer and Document Viewer window titles are translated too. In English, the Settings window title is now "App settings - Rocket.Chat". (#3663, DMV2-48)
- Click-to-call with copied phone numbers: the global call shortcut and tel:/callto: links now clean a phone number with the same rules. A (0) after a country code is removed (+49 (0)40 123456 dials +4940123456). An extension (ext. 23, x23, ;ext=) is no longer added to the number. Invisible formatting marks are removed, and full-width digits are converted. (#3662, DMV2-47)

🐛 Fixes
- Desktop notifications on workspaces that load their scripts late: on some workspaces, the app's page script ran before the web client and stopped with process is not defined. Notifications then had no reply, no action buttons and no click routing to the workspace, and the integrations that read the web client's modules stayed off. The script now runs in that case. (#3650, DSK-242)
- Logging in again after a logout: when you log out, the app clears the workspace data and reloads the page. On workspaces whose custom script blocks the page unload, that reload did not happen, and the next login could show "The application GUI just crashed" at the two-factor prompt or when the rooms loaded. The reload after a data clear now always happens. This also applies to "Clear cache", "Force reload with cache clear" and the reload after a server version change. (#3651, DSK-244)

🐛 Fixes
- Workspaces with a self-signed or private-CA certificate: the supported-versions check now accepts the certificate that you trusted for the workspace. Before, the check ignored that trust and could not get fresh supported-versions data. Then the app could show a workspace with a newer server version as "unsupported". (#3646, DSK-238)
- Workspaces behind a proxy: the supported-versions check now uses the same proxy settings as the workspace page. Before, with a proxy that only the http_proxy/https_proxy variables set, the check could not get fresh data. (#3646, SUP-1131)
- New server releases: the supported-versions data from the server or the cloud can lag behind a release. The app no longer blocks the next release after the newest listed version until the data lists it (for example, 9.1 when the data ends at 9.0). Expired exceptions and versions further ahead stay blocked. (#3646)
- Server URLs with a password that has a %: the supported-versions check now sends the password as written. (#3646)

🔧 Internal
- Fixed the upload of the macOS build artifacts to the test-build storage. (#3647)

4.19.0

✨ Improvements
- Support for the Rocket.Chat 9.0 web client: the 9.0 web client no longer includes Meteor's client packages. The desktop app used them to read the workspace state. The app now reads the window events of the web client (#3606) and the values that the web client sends through the desktop bridge (#3616). The unread badge, title, favicon, login state, user roles and Outlook credentials keep working on 9.0. Workspaces on 8.x and older keep the existing integration.
- Tray presence through the web client contract: the tray shows the status and the custom status text with its end time. It also lists the custom statuses of the workspace. This needs a server that sends the presence contract. A status that you select in the tray uses the same flow as the user menu (#3604, #3612).
- Badge from the web client: when the web client sends its own badge, the app uses it. The badge then follows the user's "Unread alert" preference (#3607).
- Electron 43.8.1: updates Electron and blocks the compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates (#3614).

🐛 Fixes
- The app keeps the bridge calls that the web client makes before the workspace finishes loading. Before, an early title change could show "The application GUI just crashed", and the favicon, title and user roles could stay empty (#3608).
- The workspace favicon loads from absolute URLs (#3610).
- After the server refuses a status change, the tray shows the real status again (#3612).
- The 8.x integration stops its setup check after setup is complete. Before, the check ran every second for the life of the page (#3613).
- The app no longer adds a store listener on each state request, and it no longer sends updates to closed windows (#3611).

🔧 Internal
- A probe for the web client window events that the desktop app reads (#3605).
- Contributor and agent documentation and tooling (#3471, #3571, #3575, #3576, #3603, #3618, #3619).

Also included
These fixes shipped earlier in the 4.18.1 to 4.18.5 patch releases:
- A workspace that starts without a network recovers when the network comes back (#3560).
- The video call window gets focus when it already shows the requested conference (#3569).
- Video calls open in the internal window on Mac App Store builds (#3570).
- Server information and settings load on Rocket.Chat 8.10, and copy works there (#3578).
- The call window closes on leave for servers that read videoCallWindow (#3581).
- Desktop notification actions report the ID of the button that the user clicked (#3582).
- Status changes fall back to users.setStatus when the server removes setUserStatus (#3583).
- Embedded players on server pages can go full screen (#3585).
- Electron 42.11.17 with the revoked eMudhra certificates blocked (#3615).

🐛 Fixes
- Leaving a video conference closes its window. On servers that read the videoCallWindow bridge name, the call window now closes when you leave the call. Before, it loaded the full Rocket.Chat app. (#3581)
- Notification action buttons report the button you clicked. The "Join" button on an incoming conference invitation now sends its own action id to the web client, so the client starts the expected action. (#3582)
- Status changes work on servers without setUserStatus. When the server no longer has the setUserStatus method, the app sets your status through users.setStatus. (#3583)
- Fullscreen works for embedded players. The fullscreen button of embedded players, such as YouTube videos in messages, now opens fullscreen on server pages. (#3585)

This is a security patch release. Update as soon as possible.
🐛 Fixes
- Distrust of the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates. The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates are public. With one of these keys, an attacker on your network can impersonate any server. This release updates Electron to 42.11.17 (Chromium 148.0.7778.280). The app now rejects certificates from these intermediates with ERR_CERT_REVOKED. (#3615)
- No trust prompt for a revoked certificate. Before, the certificate error dialog also let you trust a revoked certificate, and the app remembered that choice. The app now rejects a revoked certificate with no dialog, like Chrome. A server with a self-signed or private-CA certificate still shows the dialog. (#3615)
Details of the compromise: https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/

🐛 Fixes
- Workspaces on Rocket.Chat 8.10: the app now reads the server version from the location that Rocket.Chat 8.10 uses. Before, on these servers the app reloaded the workspace two times at startup and then turned off its desktop integrations, such as the unread badge, the server icon and title, and presence. (#3578, CORE-2792)
- Copy text and Copy link: copying from a message now works also when the app cannot finish connecting its desktop integrations to the workspace. (#3578, CORE-2792)
- Server icon and title on Rocket.Chat 7.11 and later: the workspace tab now follows changes to the server favicon and site name. The previous code did not cover the settings location that 7.11 introduced. (#3578, CORE-2792)

🐛 Fixes
- Video calls in the app on Mac App Store builds: Mac App Store builds now open video calls in the video call window. All other builds already did this. After the update, the "Video calls inside app" setting is on. You can turn it off in Settings > Video calls. (#3570, NV-88)
- Reopen a video call that is already open: the app now focuses the video call window when you open the conference that it already shows. Before, the app closed the window and opened a new one, so you left the call and joined it again. (#3569, NV-86)

🐛 Fixes
- Starting the app before the network or VPN is up no longer leaves the workspace on a gray screen. The app now shows the "Server Failed to Load" view within a few seconds. It loads the workspace as soon as the server can be reached again, without Ctrl+R. (#3560)

4.18.0

✨ Improvements
- Media indicators on workspace tabs: a tab shows when its workspace plays audio, and a click on the indicator mutes it (#3491). Tabs also show when the camera, the microphone, or screen sharing is in use (#3493).
- Find in page: press Cmd+F (macOS) or Ctrl+F (Windows and Linux) to search the text of the current workspace (#3492).
- Recovery for stuck workspaces: when a workspace stops responding or its page crashes, the app shows the failure view. The Reload button then starts the workspace again in a new process (#3533, #3556).
- Conference calls in the video call window: conference call pages now open in the video call window (#3523). The workspace can control that window through the RocketChatDesktop API (#3510).
- Settings window: the settings window now has a fixed size (#3504).
- Web UI previews (Developer Mode): load the web UI build of a Rocket.Chat pull request into a workspace (#3525, thanks @ggazzo). You can also load the build of the develop branch (#3534, thanks @ggazzo). The app keeps a history of the builds and updates them in place (#3541, #3536, #3548).

🐛 Fixes
- macOS no longer asks for screen recording permission at startup (#3552).
- go.rocket.chat deep links open the right workspace, and login matching works for http workspaces (#3518).
- Windows notification quick replies now work after the user dismisses the notification (#3519).
- "Restart to update" now quits and restarts the app on macOS (#3543).
- The conference page no longer throws errors in the video call window (#3546).
- Update channels: on the Stable channel, the app offers only stable releases. A change from the Alpha or Beta channel to Stable no longer offers an older version (#3555).

🔧 Internal
- Release builds run as one prepare job and seven parallel packaging jobs (#3513, #3532).
- Faster pull request checks: sharded Jest and transpile-only ts-jest (#3511). PR artifact builds no longer run lint and tests again (#3512, #3524).
- Removed dead code from the window migration and the video call bridge (#3514, #3515, #3516, #3517).
- engines.node matches the devEngines floor (#3502).
- Contributor and agent documentation and tooling (#3494, #3500, #3542, #3544, #3545).

Also included
These fixes shipped earlier in the 4.17.1 to 4.17.4 patch releases:
- The main window opens every time the app starts (#3535).
- An opt-in unread counter tray icon, and a macOS setting to hide the unread count in the menu bar (#3522).
- The app starts when it cannot write its configuration file (#3507).
- A way to reset saved window sizes and positions (#3488).
- The app no longer overrides the web client's presence detection on servers 7.10 and later (#3490, thanks @ricardogarim).
- Conference http(s) popups open as sandboxed child windows (#3485).
- macOS release signing fix (#3499).

🐛 Fixes
- The window now opens on every launch. If the window was hidden in the tray when the app last quit, the next launch restored that state and showed only the tray icon, which Windows can place in the notification-area overflow, so the app could look like it had not started. Launching the app now always opens the window. To start in the tray, for example from a login shortcut, add --start-hidden to the shortcut. (#3535)

🔧 Internal
- Startup logs the app version, the user data path, and how the main window's visibility was decided, to diagnose launches that show no window. (#3535)

✨ Improvements
- Unread messages in the tray icon, as an option. New setting "Unread counter in tray icon" in Settings → General. When enabled, the tray icon shows the unread badge again (a dot, 1–9 or 9+ on Windows and Linux; a dot on macOS) instead of your presence status. It's off by default, so the 4.17 presence icon stays unless you turn it on. (#3484, #3522)
- macOS: hide the unread number in the menu bar. New setting "Unread count in menu bar" (on by default) to show or hide the number next to the menu bar icon. The Dock badge is unchanged. (#3522)

🐛 Fixes
- Windows: the app no longer exits at startup when settings cannot be saved atomically. On roaming profiles with folder redirection, %APPDATA% can resolve to a network share where the safe-save rename of the settings file fails. The app previously closed before showing a window. It now falls back to a direct write so settings keep saving, starts with default settings for the session if the file still cannot be opened, and shows an error dialog with the log location if startup fails for any other reason. (#3507)

Patch release on the 4.17.x line.
🐛 Fixes
- Video calls: SSO login popups complete the redirect again. Identity-provider login popups opened from the conference window (for example Pexip SSO) now open as sandboxed Electron child windows instead of the system browser, which restores the link back to the call so the login result reaches the conference. This hardens the popup handling introduced in 4.16.0, which did not cover IdP flows that depend on window.opener. (#3485)
- Presence: users who are away stay away after a reconnection. On servers 7.10 and newer the desktop app no longer replaces the web client's own idle detection, and on every server version it re-asserts the current idle state once the websocket reconnects and login settles. Previously a scheduled websocket recycle could flip idle users back to online until the next OS idle transition. (#3490)

✨ Improvements
- Reset window sizes and positions. A new action in Settings → Advanced and in the View menu clears the remembered bounds of the main, settings, downloads, log viewer and document viewer windows and recenters them at their default size. Also fixes main-window centering on displays where the work area is not an integer. (#3488)

4.17.0

✨ Improvements
- Separate windows on a shared native shell — Log viewer, downloads, settings, and document viewer now open as independent native windows instead of in-app overlays (#3444), with follow-up correctness, performance, and UX improvements to the log viewer (#3446)
- SAML authentication through deeplink — SAML login flows can now complete via the desktop deeplink handler (#3458)
- Workspace presence in the tray — The tray icon and menu now reflect the active workspace's presence status (#3466), and hide it when the active server fails to load (#3472)

🐛 Fixes
- macOS updates now install through electron-updater, fixing manual update installs on macOS (#3431, closes #955)
- "Check for updates" now works on store builds — Mac App Store, Microsoft Store, Snap, and Flathub — pointing users to the store instead of the built-in updater (#3460)
- Windows notification quick replies are no longer lost after the toast is dismissed to the Action Center (#3464)
- Windows notification quick replies are deduplicated (#3468, thanks @Moku151)

🔧 Internal
- Release builds now trigger only on semver tags, with PR checks for release lines (#3454)
- Release tagging fails closed on unsafe tags (#3452)
- New dev/master/release branching model documented and wired into the repo guides (#3455, #3457)
- Test line coverage raised to 71.19% (#3429)

Highlights
A new workspace navigation system with three switchable layouts, a unified window chrome across all three platforms, security hardening from a 2022 pentest follow-up, and an upgrade to React 19.

✨ New workspace navigation: Tabs, Sidebar, or Titlebar
Workspace switching has been reworked into three interchangeable layouts, selectable in Settings → General or via the View menu (⌘/Ctrl+Shift+S cycles through them):
- Tabs — a horizontal browser-style tab strip with favicon, label, unread/mention badges, a keyboard-shortcut chip, drag-to-reorder, and an add-workspace button.
- Sidebar — a narrow, icon-only vertical column with square favicon tabs and badges, keyboard navigation, and improved contrast when a workspace's favicon matches the background.
- Titlebar — no sidebar and no tab strip, just the title bar with a compact server switcher.
The whole desktop chrome is now theme-aware, and the Theme selector is back in Settings. (#3424, #3394, #3419, #3413, #3403)

✨ Unified window chrome across Windows, Linux, and macOS
- Menu bar on Windows and Linux is now hidden by default — press Alt to reveal it temporarily, or pin it permanently visible from Settings → General → Menu bar, the View menu, or Ctrl+Shift+M. Existing installs are migrated automatically without overriding a choice you've already made.
- Linux now uses the same client-side window chrome as Windows: window controls embedded in the tab strip instead of relying on the desktop environment's title bar, plus softly rounded outer corners. (#3450, #3449)
- Updates are now surfaced as a titlebar label instead of a modal dialog, with clearer feedback for manual update checks and more resilient silent background checks. (#3439, #3427)
- Downloads get a new tab-strip indicator with a cleaner, more compact presentation. (#3443, #3441)
- Added a Cmd+, shortcut to open Preferences on macOS. (#3340)

🔒 Security hardening
Follow-up fixes from pentest review, tightening several areas that previously relied on broader trust than necessary:
- Restricted geolocation, notifications, and fullscreen permission prompts in the server view to trusted, configured server origins only. (CORE-1121, #3395)
- Blocked main-frame navigation to non-http(s) schemes inside the server webview. (CORE-1123, #3397)
- Tightened the Content-Security-Policy on local renderer windows. (CORE-1126, #3316)
- Session data (cookies, localStorage, indexedDB) is now cleared automatically when a user logs out of a server through the normal web app UI, not only via the manual "Clear Cache" action. (CORE-1130, #3398)
- Documented a risk-acceptance decision on certificate pinning for the auto-updater (CORE-1128) for future reference. (#3396)

🐛 Fixes
- Fixed workspace tabs intermittently getting stuck on the loading throbber after a webview boot failure — the app now recovers automatically instead of requiring a full restart. (#3436)
- Fixed a renderer infinite re-render loop that could throw "Maximum update depth exceeded". (#3435)
- Fixed an unread-badge update storm that could crash tab bar rendering, and corrected badge rendering/priority. (#3437, #3434)
- Fixed the screen-share picker appearing at app launch with no user interaction on Linux Wayland (Fedora Flatpak, Ubuntu deb) — source enumeration was running before the picker was ever opened. (#3400)
- Fixed the screen picker to show on the window that actually requested it (rather than always the main window) and to queue concurrent requests instead of dropping them. (#3399)
- Fixed screen-picker source stability under Electron 42's macOS capture stack. (#3414)
- Fixed workspaces with a valid uniqueId-scoped support exception incorrectly showing the "Unsupported" screen. (#3404, #3406, #3407)
- Fixed the sidebar tooltip showing "null" for servers beyond the 9th position. (#3326)
- Fixed the TopBar not rendering on Linux when using the Sidebar or Titlebar layouts. (#3449)
- Fixed dependency subpath imports not being externalized correctly in the Rollup build. (#3411)

🔧 Internal
- Upgraded React 18.3 → 19 and Fuselage 0.78 → 0.80. (#3384, #3383)
- Added a silent installation guide for enterprise deployments. (#3178)
- Added test coverage across preload and module boundaries. (#3393)
- Applied least-privilege permissions to GitHub Actions workflows. (#3410)
- Updated translations from Lingohub. (#3447, #3392)

🐛 Fixes
- Windows: notification reply sent duplicated (#3420) — Replying to a desktop notification from the Windows toast could send the message twice. Electron 42 enabled inline-reply events on Windows but can deliver a single reply through more than one activation path; the app now dispatches each notification reply exactly once per display cycle.

🐛 Fixes
- Video calls: first Jitsi call after a fresh install or cleared cache now joins directly instead of landing on the pre-join screen. The loading watchdog no longer interrupts slow first-time loads, and its recovery path now preserves the call's authentication token and logs its activity in production. (#3416)
- Video calls: screen sharing in the call window works again on 4.15.x — a build-pipeline gap left a react-dom/client chunk without its module wrapper (ReferenceError: exports is not defined); dependency subpath imports are now externalized and a build-time guard prevents recurrence. (#3417, backport of #3411)
- Screen sharing: picker sources stay stable under the Electron 42 macOS capture stack. (#3417, backport of #3414)
- Sidebar: fixed a crash when formatting shortcut tooltips. (#3417, backport of #3326, fixes #3244)

🐛 Fixes
- Conference deep links now open in a dedicated call window. Conference links that carry only a conference id (e.g. conference/<id>, without an explicit call URL) previously loaded the conference over the workspace webview, leaving no way back to the workspace. These links now open the conference in the standalone video call window, so closing it returns you to an untouched workspace. Links that already include an explicit call URL are unchanged. (#3412)

🔧 Internal
- CI: run pull-request build and validation workflows for hotfix/** base branches.

🐛 Fixes
- Supported-versions exceptions now validate correctly on the desktop app. Workspaces with a version exception issued by Rocket.Chat Cloud could be shown the "unsupported workspace" screen: the exception scope check did not cover deployments where the workspace uniqueID was not yet stored locally. The desktop now resolves the workspace identity before validating, and exceptions from server, cloud, and cached payloads are honored whenever they are valid and unexpired. (#3404, #3405)
- Supported-versions validation hardening. Recovery from malformed cached data no longer leaves validation in a stuck state; validation re-runs on wake from sleep; a "Check again" button on the unsupported-workspace screen re-triggers validation without restarting the app; offline validation now considers both the cached and the bundled version data, so a workspace kept usable by a cached exception is not blocked by newer bundled data. (#3405, #3406)
- Version enforcement requires complete data. A payload with a missing or malformed enforcement date no longer blocks the workspace; blocking requires a valid, past enforcement date. (#3405)
- Expiration warning reliability. The expiring-workspace warning dialog no longer fails silently when the payload's translations lack the user's language, and it re-evaluates when switching workspaces. (#3405)
- Linux/Wayland: removed startup screen-capture enumeration that could open the system screen picker when the app launched. (#3400)

🔧 Internal
- Supported-versions types and test fixtures aligned with the real /api/info contract, plus a live wire-contract test guarding against drift. (#3406)

- Internal video chat session sharing — internal conference windows now share the main webview's session, so same-origin calls load authenticated instead of hitting a login screen. Includes hardened screen-share routing, per-window call state, lifecycle bridges (close / focus-existing / open-in-main-window), and external-link routing to the system browser. (#3370)

Jitsi Video Calls Now Opening in Browser
With our latest update, we've made an important change to how video conferencing works in the Rocket.Chat Desktop application.
What's changing?
Starting with this release, all Jitsi video conferences will now open in your default web browser instead of within the Rocket.Chat Desktop app window.
Why this change?
Jitsi has recently updated their screen sharing implementation by removing support for the legacy approach we were using in our Desktop app. This change was made as part of their migration to the more modern getDisplayMedia API for screen sharing functionality, as detailed in their recent update.
Benefits of this change
- Improved stability and compatibility with Jitsi's latest features
- Better screen sharing experience through your native browser
- Full support for all Jitsi functionality without limitations
What you need to do
No action is required on your part. When you join a Jitsi video conference, it will automatically open in your default browser rather than within the Rocket.Chat Desktop application.
If you have any questions or encounter any issues with this change, please don't hesitate to reach out to our support team.
